statement: Two friends start together from the same point on a circular track 600 m long. One walks at 2 m per second and the other runs at 4 m per second, in opposite directions around the track. After how many seconds do they first meet?

choices.misconception: I used the difference of the two speeds, as if they were going the same way round.
I used only the runner's speed, as if the walker stood still.
I thought they meet when together they have covered half the track.
I averaged the two speeds to 3 m per second and divided the track length by that.

hints: Together, how much of the track have they covered when they meet?
When two people move towards each other, the gap between them closes at the sum of their speeds. Here the gap to close is the whole length of the track.
They close the 600 m gap at 2 + 4 = 6 m every second.

solutions.reliable: Moving in opposite directions, they first meet when the distances they have covered add up to the full 600 m. Together they cover 2 + 4 = 6 m each second, so they meet after 600 / 6 = 100 seconds. Check: the walker has gone 200 m and the runner 400 m, which add to 600 m. The transferable idea: when two movers approach each other, add their speeds; when one chases the other, subtract them.

whyOnTest: Meeting questions test whether speeds should be added or subtracted, and each wrong choice uses the wrong combination.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
